title: Register Programs in Randomized Logarithmic Space
statement: Let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages have a finite control-state set with decidable equality. Suppose every oracle language belongs to $	ext{LOGSPACE}$, and let $C_0,c_0$ be natural numbers and $\delta$ a positive rational. Assume that for each input $x$ there is a length $N$ such that every choice string of length $N$ makes the program halt, every pre-final configuration satisfies its validity conditions and has each register value at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$, and the following probability conditions hold: if $x\in L$, the probability of answering yes is at least $\delta$; if $x\notin L$, the probability of answering no is $1$. Then $L$ belongs to $	ext{RL}$, the class decidable by a randomized machine using logarithmic space with one-sided error.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of binary strings
The program has $m$ registers and $d$ oracle languages
The finite control-state set has decidable equality
Every oracle language is in LOGSPACE
For each input, some length $N$ makes every choice string of that length halt
Every pre-final run configuration satisfies the program's validity conditions
Every register value is at most $C_0(|x|+1)^{c_0}$
For inputs in $L$, the yes-answer probability is at least $\delta$
For inputs outside $L$, the no-answer probability is exactly $1$
